'''Ramona Amy Hoh''' (born 1979<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fis-ski.com/DB/general/athlete-biography.html?sector=AL&competitorid=25346&type=stats|title=Ramona Hoh|website=[[International Ski Federation]]|access-date=2019-12-06}}</ref>) is a Canadian former para-[[alpine skier]] from [[Edmonton]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/12-medals-for-canada-at-paralympic-games-1.165559|title=12 medals for Canada at Paralympic Games|date=1998-12-03|accessdate=2019-12-06|website=[[CBC News]]}}</ref> She won a silver and a bronze medal at the [[1994 Winter Paralympics]], and a bronze medal at the [[1998 Winter Paralympics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.paralympic.org/ramona-hoh|title= Ramona Hoh |website=[[Paralympic Games]]|accessdate=2019-12-06}}</ref>

Ramona Hoh was [[Symbrachydactyly|born without fingers on her right hand]]. She is an alumna of [[Dartmouth College]] and currently works as a molecular biologist at [[Stanford University]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dartmouthalumnimagazine.com/articles/games-changers|title=Games Changers|last=Furlong|first=Lisa|date=January–February 2010|magazine=Dartmouth Alumni Magazine|accessdate=2019-12-06}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mendeley.com/authors/55542647700/|title=Ramona Amy Hoh|website=[[Mendeley]]|accessdate=2019-12-06}}</ref> where she also received her Ph.D.<ref>{{cite thesis|last=Hoh|first=Ramona|title=The Ciliated Cell Transcriptome|date=March 2010|type=Ph.D.|publisher=[[Stanford University]]|access-date=2019-12-06|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2Y34bbyKRrEC}}</ref>
